exposure: high-risk pregnancy conditions (e.g., chronic hypertension, preeclampsia, diabetes, IUGR)
cohort: The study included 50 patients with high-risk pregnancies who underwent antepartum cardiotocography after admission.
finding: The study found that lower APGAR scores and low birth weight were significantly associated with abnormal antepartum cardiotocography.
mod_finding: There was a statistically significant difference in the method of delivery between normal and abnormal CTG groups, with abnormal CTG being associated with a higher rate of caesarean section.
birth_weight: Included babies with birth weights <2.5 kg and >2.5 kg
